picks.file: Gdynia 1942 cropped rotated RG373 445221326 F5895 ON024530 1PRU C 0256 1 46 01.jpg
picks.what: The port and city center, vertical aerial reconnaissance photograph (U.S. National Archives)
picks.why: only view of the interwar new town and port: harbor basins, rail yards, the center’s street grid and Kamienna Góra hill by the shore; trimmed the upside-down film caption

picks.what: Panorama over the city and port, photograph from the Student Seamen’s Hostel
picks.why: widest modern view: the center, the harbor and the Sea Towers on the bay

gaps: P0–P3: no candidates (Gdynia was a village until the 1920s). P4: only a manor house in Mały Kack (#1), not the town. P6 has no Quality image.
notes: #2 is a black-and-white vertical air photo (wartime, when the city was German-occupied ‘Gotenhafen’), so it reads somewhat like a map; drop it if a plain photograph is wanted. ‘1PRU’ in the file name suggests an RAF No. 1 Photographic Reconnaissance Unit sortie. P6 alternatives: #6 (CC0, Sea Towers behind a cargo ship that dominates the frame), #4/#5 (Redłowo district only).
